correctness.rationale: The source-limited exact W2+KL scalar problem reduces by Cauchy-Schwarz and maximum-entropy inequalities to a strictly convex positive quadratic root. Differentiation gives the exact optimizer derivative, monotonic derivative limit, and hence the optimal Lipschitz factor q<1; the completed closed orthant yields a unique positive fixed point. The envelope Hessian gives the sharp 2(1-q) strong convexity. Uniform contraction in outlier scale gives the finite limit; analytic implicit differentiation at delta=tau/M² yields K/M²+O(M^-4); scalar 1/b asymptotics yield sqrt(1-w)B_w ->sqrt(a²+tau/2). All quantifiers, constant normalizations and boundary/limit order were checked. The independent standard-library checker passed 7366 deterministic assertions after source-file replay; numerical experiments alone prove no global statement.

originality.rationale: The first-publicly-submitted 2024 primary source proves Gaussian semi-unbalanced reduction and supplies the hybrid optimizer, while its Theorem 6 and Appendix D.3 provide qualitative convergence under an assumed compact spectral strip, not the optimal all-start commuting-submanifold contraction. The current result adds the exact full-domain Lipschitz and strong-convexity moduli, an analytically finite single-covariance-outlier response, an exact inverse-square correction, and a near-total-contamination square-root exponent. Closely relevant 2026 revised and conference sources and established Gaussian barycenter literature were checked to the extent stated; a conference PDF could not be read, leaving a priority risk.
residual_risks: The later 2026 conference version of the same-author paper was not materially read beyond its abstract because the PDF endpoint was inaccessible; the freely accessible updated arXiv full text was inspected, but it need not be identical.
Unindexed or other specialized one-sided Gaussian KL-barycenter literature may contain equivalent scalar formulas. A negative search is not definitive independent publication-priority certification.
The commuting restriction is mathematically substantial; results should not be extrapolated to noncommuting covariance matrices or unconstrained non-Gaussian measures.

value.rationale: The precise input-dependent optimal q and global start-free convergence removes the restrictive compact-iterate condition from a motivated exact Gaussian semi-unbalanced hybrid algorithm in the commuting case, providing a usable stopping/rate benchmark. The finite covariance-outlier ceiling, sharp inverse-square approach and degeneration as clean weight vanishes quantify the model’s numerical/statistical robustness boundary and contrast with ordinary Wasserstein barycenters. These are structurally motivated and not arbitrary finite slices; no noncommuting algorithm guarantee or non-Gaussian contamination claim is made.
